name: The Fool
upright: A fresh start with more heart than map. The Fool packs light, grins at the cliff edge and steps forward anyway. Say yes to the new thing, and let yourself be a beginner.
reversed: Hesitation, or a leap taken without looking at the ground. Check your pockets, tie your shoes, then go. Holding back out of fear and rushing out of boredom can look alike.
reflect: What would I try this week if I were allowed to be bad at it?

name: The Magician
label: I
upright: Everything you need is already on the table. This card is about turning an idea into an action with the tools in reach: your hands, your words, your attention. Pick one thing and begin.
reversed: Talent scattered across too many projects, or charm used to dodge the real work. Gather your tools back to one spot and be straight about what you are making.
reflect: What is the one thing I could start today with what I already have?

name: The High Priestess
label: II
upright: Sit quietly and listen to the part of you that knows before it can explain. Not everything needs answering today. Some answers arrive only when you stop asking out loud.
reversed: The inner voice is muffled by noise, or you are hiding a truth from yourself. Turn the volume down on other people's opinions and take a long, honest pause.
reflect: What do I already suspect that I have not said out loud?

name: The Empress
label: III
upright: Generous, fertile and unhurried. The Empress asks you to enjoy the garden you have been tending: good food, soft light, a body that is looked after. Make room for lush, slow things.
reversed: Giving until you are empty, or letting a creative well go dry. Receive as well as give. Take a day to be cared for, and tend yourself first.
reflect: Where could I be gentler with my own needs?

name: The Emperor
label: IV
upright: A sturdy frame that holds things up. This card favors clear rules, reliable habits and calm authority that protects instead of bossing. Build the scaffolding your good ideas need.
reversed: Control that has gone stiff, or structure that has gone missing. Ask whether a rule still serves anyone, and where a little firmness would actually bring relief.
reflect: Which boundary would make everything else easier to carry?

name: The Hierophant
label: V
upright: Wisdom handed down, and the comfort of doing something the way it has long been done. Seek a mentor, a community or a practice with deep roots, and notice what you want to keep.
reversed: Time to question a rule you inherited, or to find your own way of doing a ritual. You can honor where you come from and still change the recipe.
reflect: Which tradition do I love, and which one am I only carrying out of habit?

name: The Lovers
label: VI
upright: A meaningful choice made with an open heart. It is about love, yes, but also about what you value and who you want to be when you choose. Alignment feels like relief.
reversed: Friction between what you say and what you want, or a choice you keep postponing. Get clear on your values first, and the decision gets lighter.
reflect: What does my choice say about what I care about most?

name: The Chariot
label: VII
upright: Two strong pulls, one steady hand. You can move forward by holding opposing urges in balance rather than fighting them. Pick a direction, set your jaw and roll.
reversed: The wheels spin without grip, or you are charging ahead with no destination. Slow down, check the map, and make sure you are steering rather than being dragged.
reflect: Where do I actually want to be going, and what is pulling me off course?

name: Strength
label: VIII
upright: The kind of strength that does not need to shout. You tame the wild thing, in the world or in yourself, with patience and a steady, kind hand. Gentleness is a form of nerve.
reversed: Doubt is louder than usual, or you are forcing a result that needs time. Remember what you have already gotten through, and approach the problem with softness.
reflect: Where would a gentle approach work better than a forceful one?

name: The Hermit
label: IX
upright: Step away from the crowd and carry a small light a little further. Time alone is not loneliness here, it is how you hear yourself. What you find may help someone else later.
reversed: Solitude has curdled into isolation, or you are avoiding people because it is easier. Reach out to one trusted person and let the lantern light two faces.
reflect: What do I need quiet for, and who could I invite back in afterwards?

name: Wheel of Fortune
label: X
upright: The wheel turns, as it always does. A shift of circumstance may be underway, and the best response is to stay flexible, notice the pattern and use the moment while it is here.
reversed: A stuck stretch, or resistance to something already in motion. Not every low point is a verdict. Hold on to your center and wait for the next turn.
reflect: What cycle am I in, and what is it trying to teach me?

name: Justice
label: XI
upright: Weigh things honestly and decide with a clear head. This card likes plain facts, fair terms and owning your part. A balanced choice now saves a tangled one later.
reversed: Bias in the scales, or a hard truth being avoided. Look again for what you left out, including your own role, and be as fair to yourself as you would be to a friend.
reflect: What would I decide if I weighed this exactly the way I would for someone else?

name: The Hanged One
label: XII
upright: A deliberate pause that changes your point of view. Hang upside down for a bit and the same old problem looks different. Release the urge to push and see what shifts.
reversed: Stalling for the sake of it, or making a sacrifice nobody asked you to make. If waiting has stopped teaching you anything, it may be time to climb down.
reflect: What looks different if I turn the problem upside down?

name: Death
label: XIII
upright: An ending that makes space, not a literal one. A chapter closes, a habit falls away, a role is outgrown. Honor it, take what you learned and let the ground rest before planting again.
reversed: Clinging to something that is already over, or dragging out a goodbye. Change is easier when you stop bargaining with it. What are you ready to put down?
reflect: What has already ended that I am still carrying around?

name: Temperance
label: XIV
upright: A little of this, a little of that, mixed with care. The card favors the middle path, steady pacing and bringing different parts of life into harmony. Slow blending makes a better brew.
reversed: Too much, too fast, or everything out of proportion. Go back to the basics of sleep, food and simple routines, and re-measure what you are pouring in.
reflect: What am I overdoing right now, and what is getting too little?

name: The Devil
label: XV
upright: Look at what has you hooked: a habit, a belief, a person, a screen. The chains here are loose enough to lift off. Naming the pull honestly is the first move toward choosing again.
reversed: The grip is loosening. You see the pattern and you are starting to step out of it. Be patient with yourself, and ask a friend to help hold the door.
reflect: What do I keep going back to that I secretly wish I could put down?

name: The Tower
label: XVI
upright: Something built on shaky ground comes down, and fresh air rushes in. It is jarring, and often it is also a relief. Take shelter, stay kind to yourself and keep the useful bricks.
reversed: A shake-up that is avoided, delayed or already underway quietly. Pay attention to the small cracks now, and make changes before the weather forces them.
reflect: What is already wobbling that I have been pretending is fine?

name: The Star
label: XVII
upright: After the storm comes a clear night. This card points to gentle recovery, honest hope and the courage to be seen as you are. Small, steady offerings add up to something real.
reversed: Hope feels thin and you may be running on fumes. Rest first. Look for one small thing that still glimmers and start there, with no big plan required.
reflect: Where could I pour a little patience, and what would help me believe it will fill back up?

name: The Moon
label: XVIII
upright: Things are not quite what they seem by moonlight, and that is okay. Follow your intuition, pay attention to your dreams and move carefully through the fog without insisting on certainty.
reversed: The fog begins to thin. A worry loses its shape, or something hidden comes into view. Check what is real, and let go of the fears that only live in the dark.
reflect: What am I imagining the worst about, and what do I actually know?

name: The Sun
label: XIX
upright: Plain, unembarrassed gladness. Things are lit up and easy to see, and your energy has somewhere good to go. Say thank you, share the good news and soak in the warmth.
reversed: Clouds drift over, or you are playing it too cool to enjoy a win. Joy still counts when it is small. Let yourself have a bright spot today.
reflect: What would feel like sunshine on an ordinary day?

name: Judgement
label: XX
upright: A clear call to rise and become who you have been getting ready to be. Look back with kindness, forgive what you can, and answer the part of you that has been waiting to be heard.
reversed: Self-criticism drowns out the call, or you are pressing snooze on something important. You are allowed to forgive your past self and begin again.
reflect: What is quietly calling me, and what am I doing to avoid answering it?

name: The World
label: XXI
upright: A cycle completes and you get to look at the whole picture. Take a victory lap and say thanks to everyone who helped. The end of one journey is also the doorway to the next.
reversed: Almost there, with a loose thread left to tie. Do not skip the last bit. Finish it with care and the whole thing will feel properly done.
reflect: What have I finished that I never properly celebrated?

name: Ace of Wands
label: Ace
upright: A spark of fresh energy and a good idea that will not leave you alone. Strike the match while it is lit and see what catches.
reversed: The spark flickers: a project stalls or enthusiasm runs dry. Check whether you need rest, a smaller first step, or a different idea.
reflect: What idea keeps tapping me on the shoulder?

name: Two of Wands
label: Two
upright: You hold the world in your hand and look out at the horizon. Time to plan: pick a direction and decide how far you want to go.
reversed: Staying in the safe castle, or planning without ever packing. Fear of the unknown can keep a good plan stuck on paper.
reflect: What would I start if I trusted myself to figure out the rest on the way?

name: Three of Wands
label: Three
upright: Your first efforts are set in motion and now you watch for what sails in. Keep an eye on the horizon and think about the next stage.
reversed: Delays, or a plan that did not travel as expected. Adjust the route rather than the destination, and ask for help where you need it.
reflect: What have I set going that I could simply let develop?

name: Four of Wands
label: Four
upright: A reason to put up the bunting. A milestone, a homecoming or a steady patch worth enjoying. Gather your people and mark it.
reversed: Uneasy at home, or a celebration that feels a little hollow. Ask what would make the place feel like yours again.
reflect: What deserves a small party this week?

name: Five of Wands
label: Five
upright: A lively tangle of opinions and egos, like five people holding five different maps. Healthy rivalry can sharpen ideas, so long as it stays playful.
reversed: Conflict eases or goes underground. Pick your battles, and look for the point everyone actually agrees on.
reflect: Is this a real disagreement or just a loud one?

name: Six of Wands
label: Six
upright: A public win and a well-earned cheer. Accept the applause, thank your supporters and let yourself feel proud.
reversed: Waiting for credit that does not arrive, or letting ego write the story. Do it for the work, and let the recognition find its own timing.
reflect: What accomplishment have I been brushing off?

name: Seven of Wands
label: Seven
upright: You hold the high ground and stick to your position, even when it feels like everyone is pushing back. Stand firm on what matters.
reversed: Feeling overwhelmed and outnumbered. Is every hill worth defending? Choose one and ask for backup.
reflect: What am I defending, and does it still deserve my energy?

name: Eight of Wands
label: Eight
upright: Everything speeds up. Messages arrive, plans move and the path clears. Ride the momentum, and keep your eyes on where things land.
reversed: Crossed wires and traffic jams. Slow down, re-check the details and avoid hitting send in a rush.
reflect: What needs a quick answer, and what can wait until tomorrow?

name: Nine of Wands
label: Nine
upright: Bruised but still on your feet, with one more push to go. You have come too far to quit now, so lean on what you have learned.
reversed: Running on empty or guarded to the point of exhaustion. Put some weight down. Not every wall needs to stay up.
reflect: What have I been carrying alone that I could hand off?

name: Ten of Wands
label: Ten
upright: You have taken on a lot and the bundle is heavy. Check whether every stick in it is yours, and see which can be set down or shared.
reversed: Dropping a load at last, or collapsing under it. Delegate, simplify and let some things go undone.
reflect: What is the first thing I could take off my list?

name: Page of Wands
label: Page
upright: A bright, curious beginner with news or a new idea. Try things out, ask questions and let yourself be enthusiastic.
reversed: Big plans and little follow-through, or a sulky creative block. Start small and play without worrying how it looks.
reflect: What would I try if nobody was watching?

name: Knight of Wands
label: Knight
upright: Dashing off after a goal at full speed. Energetic, charismatic and a bit restless. Great for kickstarting, so long as you look where you are going.
reversed: Burning out or bolting at the first obstacle. Look for a pace you can keep up for more than a weekend.
reflect: Where is my enthusiasm ahead of my plan?

name: Queen of Wands
label: Queen
upright: Warm, confident and welcoming, someone who lights up a room by being comfortable in it. Draw on your own spark and bring others in.
reversed: Dimmed confidence or a short fuse. Check what is draining you and take back your own warmth before offering it to others.
reflect: What makes me feel most like myself?

name: King of Wands
label: King
upright: A visionary who inspires by example and knows how to turn a dream into a team effort. Lead with warmth and clear aims.
reversed: A big personality running over the quiet ones, or plans that outpace patience. Listen before you launch the next idea.
reflect: How can I lead in a way that makes room for others?

name: Ace of Cups
label: Ace
upright: A cup brimming with fresh feeling: a new friendship, a spark of affection or a sudden softening. Let it fill, and let yourself receive.
reversed: A closed or empty cup. Feelings may be blocked or held back. Be gentle and let the water find a way again in its own time.
reflect: What feeling am I ready to let in?

name: Two of Cups
label: Two
upright: Two people meeting as equals, with a spark of mutual respect. A friendship, collaboration or romance where both sides pour in.
reversed: Lopsided give-and-take, or a misread signal. Say what you need plainly, and listen for what the other person needs too.
reflect: Where could I use a little more give-and-take?

name: Three of Cups
label: Three
upright: Good company shaped this chapter. A shared table, a toast, people who make the hard parts lighter. Notice who you want to keep close.
reversed: Too much party or a clique that shuts others out. Check whether the company is feeding you or just filling time.
reflect: Who do I want at my next table?

name: Four of Cups
label: Four
upright: A pause with arms folded while a gift is quietly offered. You may be bored, or weighing options. Look up and see what is actually on the table.
reversed: Waking up from the fog and noticing what you want. Say yes to something real, even a small thing.
reflect: What am I overlooking because I am so busy looking elsewhere?

name: Five of Cups
label: Five
upright: Three cups have spilled and it is tempting to stare at them. Honor the sadness, then turn around: two cups still stand behind you.
reversed: Starting to move on, picking up what is left and walking toward the bridge. Grief softens when you give it room.
reflect: What is still standing that I have not looked at yet?

name: Six of Cups
label: Six
upright: A warm wave of memory, old friends and simple kindness. Revisit what made you happy, and share some of that sweetness today.
reversed: Living in the past, or an old story that no longer fits. Honor the memory, then see what the present has to offer.
reflect: Which memory could I borrow a little comfort from?

name: Seven of Cups
label: Seven
upright: A shelf full of shiny possibilities and a mind running a hundred scenarios. Enjoy the dreaming, then choose one thing to try in real life.
reversed: The mist lifts and a clearer choice appears. Trim the list, and settle on what you truly want.
reflect: Which dream is worth turning into a plan?

name: Eight of Cups
label: Eight
upright: You leave something that is no longer enough, heading toward a deeper kind of fulfillment. Leaving can be a loving act toward yourself.
reversed: Hesitating at the edge, or drifting from thing to thing without landing. Look for what you are really searching for.
reflect: What am I ready to leave, and what am I walking toward?

name: Nine of Cups
label: Nine
upright: A wish come true or a quiet sense of 'this is enough'. Savor what is good, and say thank you out loud.
reversed: Chasing a feeling instead of enjoying the real thing, or smug comfort. Check whether you are satisfied or only distracted.
reflect: What is already enough right now?

name: Ten of Cups
label: Ten
upright: A rainbow over a happy home. Family, chosen or born into, doing well together. Feeling at ease in the people and place around you.
reversed: Strain at home, or an ideal picture that does not match real life. Talk honestly and give belonging time to grow.
reflect: What would make my home feel more like a home?

name: Page of Cups
label: Page
upright: A gentle, dreamy messenger with something surprising in the cup. A heartfelt note, a new creative impulse or an open curiosity.
reversed: Oversensitive or a mood that tips quickly. Journal it out and be kind to the tender parts.
reflect: What small, soft impulse should I follow?

name: Knight of Cups
label: Knight
upright: A romantic and thoughtful visitor with an offer or invitation. Follow your heart, with your eyes open.
reversed: Moody or too good to be true. Look past the charm to what is actually being offered.
reflect: Am I falling for a person or for a picture of them?

name: Queen of Cups
label: Queen
upright: A deep well of compassion and understanding. Trust your intuition and offer a listening ear, while keeping something for yourself.
reversed: Soaking up everyone's feelings until you cannot find your own. Set a gentle boundary and refill your cup first.
reflect: Whose feelings am I carrying that are not mine?

name: King of Cups
label: King
upright: Calm waters on a rolling sea. Someone who feels deeply and responds with wisdom. Be the steady voice in the room.
reversed: Bottled-up feelings or moodiness hidden behind a smile. Let some of the water out, in a safe place.
reflect: How can I be both honest and kind right now?

name: Ace of Swords
label: Ace
upright: A sudden clear thought that cuts through the fog. Say the true thing plainly. Clear words and a sharp new idea are on offer.
reversed: Muddled thinking or words that wound more than they help. Slow down, sharpen the question and try again.
reflect: What do I see clearly now that I could not see last week?

name: Two of Swords
label: Two
upright: Torn between two options with a blindfold on. Take it off, gather what you know and admit what you feel. A pause is fine, an endless one is not.
reversed: The pressure to choose is rising, or information is spilling out. Face the facts and make a decision you can live with.
reflect: What am I refusing to look at?

name: Three of Swords
label: Three
upright: A tender wound, a hard conversation or a disappointment. It hurts because it matters. Let yourself feel it and be gentle while it heals.
reversed: The ache starts to ease, or you are holding it in. Forgive what you can, and let time do its patient work.
reflect: What do I need to hear from myself right now?

name: Four of Swords
label: Four
upright: A proper rest after a hard stretch. Step back, recharge and let your mind be quiet for a bit. Recovery is part of the work.
reversed: Restlessness or refusing to slow down. Your body and mind are asking for a break. Take one.
reflect: What would genuine rest look like this week?

name: Five of Swords
label: Five
upright: A win that costs more than it is worth. Ask what you actually want from this argument, and consider letting the other side keep their sword.
reversed: Making peace or finally dropping an old fight. Apologies and compromises start to feel possible.
reflect: Would I rather be right or be at peace?

name: Six of Swords
label: Six
upright: A quiet crossing from rough water to calmer shores. Bring only what you need, and trust that things are easing.
reversed: Hard to leave, or the journey keeps getting delayed. Name what you are afraid to bring along, or to leave.
reflect: What am I ready to carry across, and what can stay behind?

name: Seven of Swords
label: Seven
upright: A sly, resourceful plan, or the temptation to take a shortcut. Think about what you can do on your own terms, and be honest about the cost.
reversed: Coming clean, or getting found out. Honesty is simpler to carry than a cover story.
reflect: What am I keeping quiet that I might do better to share?

name: Eight of Swords
label: Eight
upright: The ropes are looser than they look. You feel boxed in, but the story that you are trapped may be doing more work than the actual walls. Take a step.
reversed: The bindings fall away as you realize you had options all along. Move at your own pace, and ask someone to hold the door.
reflect: What if the way out is simpler than I think?

name: Nine of Swords
label: Nine
upright: Night worries that grow in the dark. You are not alone with them. Say them aloud to a friend, write them down, and give yourself some kindness.
reversed: The worry is easing, or you are ready to ask for help. Dawn does arrive, even when the night is long.
reflect: Is this worry telling me something, or only repeating itself?

name: Ten of Swords
label: Ten
upright: The worst is behind you: a painful chapter has come to a full stop. Notice the sunrise on the horizon. The only way from here is up.
reversed: Hanging on to a drama that has already finished. You can stand up now. Let the dawn do its work.
reflect: What can I finally call finished?

name: Page of Swords
label: Page
upright: A quick-witted student with questions and a notebook. Stay curious, ask what you are wondering and read widely.
reversed: Gossip, sharp words or all talk. Check your facts, and think before you speak.
reflect: What question have I been too shy to ask?

name: Knight of Swords
label: Knight
upright: A fast, focused mind charging at an idea. Great for solving a problem, as long as you remember there are people on the receiving end.
reversed: Rushing in, or arguing for sport. Pause and see who you are talking over.
reflect: Where is my certainty running ahead of my listening?

name: Queen of Swords
label: Queen
upright: Clear-eyed, straight-talking and fair. She sees through fuss and tells it like it is, with grace. Say what you mean, and mean what you say.
reversed: Coldness or cutting remarks. Remember that sharp can be gentle too. Soften the delivery, keep the honesty.
reflect: What is the kindest honest thing I could say?

name: King of Swords
label: King
upright: A clear head and a steady voice. Weigh the facts, set fair rules and speak with calm authority.
reversed: Cold logic, or rules for rules' sake. Check whether you are leading with your head at the expense of your heart.
reflect: Where might a little empathy improve my argument?

name: Ace of Pentacles
label: Ace
upright: A solid, tangible beginning, like a seed in good soil. A new craft, home, routine or chance to build something real. Plant it and tend it.
reversed: A missed opening, or a plan with shaky roots. Look at what the idea needs to grow, and be patient with the setup.
reflect: What small, real thing could I begin to build?

name: Two of Pentacles
label: Two
upright: Keeping two things in motion at once and enjoying the rhythm. Stay flexible, and let yourself prioritize.
reversed: Dropping a ball or spreading too thin. Choose what matters most today and let the rest wobble.
reflect: What can I put down for a while?

name: Three of Pentacles
label: Three
upright: Skills meeting in a shared project. Each person brings a piece, and the whole is better for it. Ask for feedback and offer your craft.
reversed: Mismatched effort or a group that is not pulling together. Clarify roles and expectations, kindly.
reflect: Who could I learn from, and who could I teach?

name: Four of Pentacles
label: Four
upright: Guarding what you have, and for good reason. Stability matters, so long as the grip is not so tight that nothing new can come in.
reversed: Loosening up, or spending without thinking. Find a comfortable middle between hoarding and scattering.
reflect: What am I clutching that I could hold more lightly?

name: Five of Pentacles
label: Five
upright: A cold patch where it feels like everyone else is inside. Help is closer than it seems. Knock on the lit window and ask.
reversed: Things are starting to thaw. A hand is held out, or you are ready to accept one. Recovery begins with a small step.
reflect: Who could I ask for support, even in a small way?

name: Six of Pentacles
label: Six
upright: Giving and receiving in fair measure. Share what you have, or accept what is offered, without strings attached.
reversed: A lopsided arrangement. Notice who is always giving and who is always taking, and adjust.
reflect: Where could I give or receive a little more freely?

name: Seven of Pentacles
label: Seven
upright: You have done the planting and now you wait. Pause to look at what has grown and what needs tending. Growth takes the time it takes.
reversed: Impatience or effort that has not paid off yet. Rethink the approach, or give it another season.
reflect: What am I tending that deserves more patience?

name: Eight of Pentacles
label: Eight
upright: Hammering away at your craft, one piece at a time. Mastery is built from small, repeated, careful efforts. Enjoy the rhythm.
reversed: Boredom, perfectionism or half-hearted effort. Try a new angle on the routine, or revisit why you started.
reflect: What would I like to get quietly, steadily better at?

name: Nine of Pentacles
label: Nine
upright: A well-earned moment in your own garden. You made this life, and it is allowed to feel good. Enjoy your own company.
reversed: Overworking to prove something, or enjoying the garden without noticing it. Check what 'enough' means to you.
reflect: What have I built that I have not paused to enjoy?

name: Ten of Pentacles
label: Ten
upright: Long-lasting foundations, a family, a lineage or a community that spans generations. Think about what you want to pass on, in love and habit as well as in things.
reversed: Tension over inheritance, expectation or tradition. Choose which parts of the family story to carry forward.
reflect: What would I like to leave behind that is not an object?

name: Page of Pentacles
label: Page
upright: A student of the practical: someone who studies carefully and takes a small step at a time. Learn a new skill and enjoy the process.
reversed: Daydreaming without doing, or putting off a first step. Pick one tiny task and do it.
reflect: What new skill have I been meaning to start?

name: Knight of Pentacles
label: Knight
upright: Slow and steady wins. Methodical, dependable and willing to do the unglamorous bits. Keep your pace and you will get there.
reversed: Stuck in a rut or too cautious to move. Change one small thing in the routine.
reflect: Where is steady good enough, and where does it need a spark?

name: Queen of Pentacles
label: Queen
upright: A caring, resourceful host who makes a home from whatever is on hand. Look after the people and places you love, and yourself too.
reversed: Overextended caretaking, or neglecting the body and home. Refill your own tea cup.
reflect: What would help my space feel more nourishing?

name: King of Pentacles
label: King
upright: A steady provider who has built something good and shares it. Calm, reliable and generous. Enjoy the results of long effort.
reversed: Stubbornness or valuing things over people. Check whether the garden has become a fence.
reflect: How can I use what I have built to help others?
